title: Grid placement and named areas
learningObjectives: Explain grid placement and named areas and use CSS Grid to create responsive two-dimensional layouts.

understand.concept: Grid items can be placed using grid-column, grid-row, line numbers, spans, and named grid lines. grid-template-areas provides a readable map of named layout regions, while grid-area assigns an item to a named area.
understand.whyItMatters: Explicit placement helps build dashboards and page shells. Ensure the visual arrangement does not create a confusing reading or focus order that differs from the DOM order.
understand.analogy: Named areas are like labelled rooms on a floor plan; each component is assigned to a named region.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; CSS Grid follows formal track sizing, placement, and alignment algorithms.

explain.narrative: Each semantic region is assigned to a named area. The visual map is explicit and easy to inspect.

questions.prompt: Which property defines the named layout map for a grid?
questions.explanation: grid-template-areas declares the named grid areas and their arrangement.

questions.prompt: What should a responsive Grid layout preserve?
options: Readable content and logical DOM order
A fixed number of columns at every width
Visual placement regardless of keyboard order
questions.answer: Readable content and logical DOM order
questions.explanation: Responsive layout should adapt while preserving access and meaningful reading order.
